solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Second-hand American edition

explanation.surface: A used copy of a book published in the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Something second-hand has already had an owner, so it is not new but pre-owned.

clue.text: Small component and mostly simple

parts.note: a part is a component

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its final letter, leaving most of it

explanation.surface: A small part that is also mostly straightforward to fit.
explanation.definitionFit: Spartan living is austere and plain, without comforts, as in ancient Sparta.

clue.text: Trance from taking ecstasy in a shot of whisky?

indicators.note: taking means the dram takes in the drug, holding it inside

parts.note: a dram is a small measure of whisky
E is the slang abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Dazed after spiking a whisky with an ecstasy pill.
explanation.definitionFit: A dream is a reverie, a state of being lost in thought like a trance.

clue.text: Spot old feline is trapped by a big one

indicators.note: being trapped by something means being held inside it, so the old feline sits within the big one

parts.note: a big feline, following on from feline, is a lion
a cat is a feline

explanation.surface: An ageing cat cornered by a lion, seen as a dramatic moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a big one' refers back to 'feline': it means a big cat, not a large spot, and that big cat is split open to hold the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A spot in the sense of a place or site is a location.

clue.text: Swimming pool disposing of old cover

indicators.note: disposing of means getting rid of a letter from the pool's name

parts.note: a lido is an open-air public swimming pool

explanation.surface: An old pool cover being thrown away by the baths.
explanation.walkthrough: A lido is a British term for an outdoor public swimming pool.
explanation.definitionFit: A lid is a removable top that closes a container.

clue.text: Relative supporting estate, say, with billions for architectural eyesore

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting puts the relative underneath the rest

parts.note: an estate is a type of car, a station wagon
an uncle is a relative

explanation.surface: A relation funding an estate with billions to build an ugly monstrosity.
explanation.walkthrough: An estate car is the British name for a station wagon. Prince Charles famously called a planned National Gallery extension a 'monstrous carbuncle'.
explanation.definitionFit: A carbuncle, originally a boil, came to mean an ugly building after a royal speech.

clue.text: Could this one have every individual in term losing marks?

definitions.text: Could this one have every individual in term losing marks?

indicators.note: in places every individual inside the shortened term
losing means a letter is removed from term

parts.note: taken as written
M is the abbreviation for marks, as in the old German currency
each means every individual one

explanation.surface: Asks whether a school figure might have the whole class losing marks this term.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue also describes the person who sets and grades pupils' work, which is why it ends with a question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A schoolmaster could give every pupil in a term poorer marks, which is the clue's picture.

clue.text: Constellation — or moon of Jupiter given name?

parts.note: Io is one of the large moons of Jupiter

explanation.surface: Asks whether a star group is really a named moon of Jupiter.
explanation.definitionFit: Orion, the hunter, is a prominent group of stars in the night sky.

clue.text: Year's plan is clear and organised

indicators.note: organised suggests the letters of clear and are arranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A tidy, well-ordered annual schedule is easy to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A calendar lays out the days and months of a year, a chart of the year ahead.

clue.text: Cab's losing time as something running through wheel

indicators.note: losing tells us a letter is dropped from the word for cabs

parts.note: cabs are taxis; the 's is read as the plural

explanation.surface: A taxi losing time because something has gone wrong with its wheels.
explanation.walkthrough: Cab's is read as cabs, plural: TAXIS without its T.
explanation.definitionFit: An axle or spindle passes through the centre of a wheel, the line around which it rotates.

clue.text: Half the alphabet? This was split some time ago

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read cryptically: the first half of the alphabet runs from A to M, written as three words

definitions.text: This was split some time ago
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the particle whose nucleus physicists first split in 1932

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is a pun: spoken as 'A to M' it names the alphabet's first half; the second sense is the real definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Physicists first split the nucleus of this tiny particle in 1932, a famous scientific milestone.

clue.text: Smashing beginning to Cheltenham racing

indicators.note: the beginning to a word is its first letter

parts.note: racing means rushing, going at speed

explanation.surface: A great start to the Cheltenham horse racing festival.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheltenham is an English racecourse, home of a famous jumps festival; the surface uses 'Smashing' as praise for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Crushing and smashing both mean breaking something into pieces by force, or a decisive overwhelming win.

clue.text: So cereals must be mixed in dish

indicators.note: must be mixed tells us the letters of so cereals are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction to stir cereals into a dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A casserole is a covered pot, and the stew slowly cooked in it.

clue.text: A short distance from Winchester

definitions.note: a plural noun phrase in use: something only inches away is a short distance off

indicators.note: from signals that the letters are taken out of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Someone who lives just a little way out of the city of Winchester.
explanation.walkthrough: Winchester is an English cathedral city; the answer sits inside its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Inches are small units of length, so a few inches is a very small span.

clue.text: Gathering of crops is most tough with little volume brought in for days

indicators.note: brought in for means one letter takes the place of another

parts.note: hardest means most tough
V is the short form of volume

explanation.surface: Bringing in crops is the toughest job, with little time to spare.
explanation.walkthrough: In HARDEST the D (days) is replaced by V (volume).
explanation.definitionFit: The harvest is the season's reaping of ripe grain and produce from the fields.

clue.text: Dog we left to run back for bird

parts.note: a cur is a dog, especially a mongrel

indicators.note: running back means the letters of we plus left are read in reverse

explanation.surface: A dog we let off the lead chases back after a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The curlew is a wading bird with a long downcurved bill.

clue.text: Intrinsic quality of German city church

parts.note: Essen is a city in the Ruhr region of Germany
CE is the abbreviation for the Church of England

explanation.surface: The defining character of a particular German city's church.
explanation.definitionFit: The essence of something is its fundamental nature, the core of what it is.

clue.text: Show mercy to viper coiled in tree, heading off

indicators.note: in places the coiled snake's letters within the shortened tree
heading off means the first letter of the word is removed
coiled suggests the letters of viper are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: Sparing a snake found wound round the branch of a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coiled' looks like it describes the snake's posture, but it signals the shuffle; the tree is not the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To reprieve someone is to cancel or delay their punishment, an act of clemency.

clue.text: Added text rarely shows

indicators.note: shows means the answer is on display within the words text rarely

explanation.surface: An addendum to a document that seldom appears.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra means additional, over and above what was there before.

clue.text: Don't hit silly young girl

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to fail to strike a target
second meaning: a ... is a girl, often a pert or silly one

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as an instruction not to strike a child; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both failing to strike the target and a young unmarried girl.

clue.text: Warrant queen held in hand — not the last

indicators.note: held in means the queen is placed inside the shortened hand
not the last means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: mitt is slang for a hand
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the standard crossword queen

explanation.surface: A royal warrant clutched in the hand, with something missing at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Warrant' looks like a noun, a legal document, but here it is the verb: to deserve.
explanation.definitionFit: To merit something is to deserve or justify it, as when actions warrant a response.

clue.text: Swelling troubling your eyelid, primarily

indicators.note: primarily means taking the first letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: A painful lump bothering you on the edge of your eyelid.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does both jobs: its leading letters spell the answer and it describes one.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed infected bump on the rim of an eyelid.

clue.text: Bidding not working with European cartel

parts.note: a machine that is off is not working
a ring is a group of traders fixing prices, a cartel

explanation.surface: A bid that collapses because a European price-fixing cartel is involved.
explanation.definitionFit: A bidding at auction is an offering, the amount put forward for an item.

clue.text: Football Association gets new supporter

parts.note: FA is the abbreviation for the Football Association, which governs English football

explanation.surface: The football authority gains a new backer.
explanation.definitionFit: A fan is an enthusiastic follower of a team or performer.

clue.text: God being shown around the temple

indicators.note: around tells us the piece for being shown goes round to the far side of the, so it comes last

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of the wild
a film or play that is on is being shown

explanation.surface: A deity's image is displayed to visitors touring a temple.
explanation.walkthrough: Pan is the goat-legged Greek god of shepherds.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pantheon in Rome is a famous ancient temple to all the gods.

clue.text: Row when stopwatch loses minutes?

indicators.note: loses says a letter is dropped from the word for stopwatch

parts.note: a stopwatch is a timer

explanation.surface: An argument breaks out because the stopwatch has lost time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel; here it means a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is one rank in a series of rows, such as raised seats in a stadium.
